title: Streamline crypto bindings and unify SSO assertion parsing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Reduce tech debt across authentication libraries by consolidating native crypto bindings, upgrading OpenSSL to a vetted 3.x build with FIPS toggles for Private customers, and standardizing JWT and SAML parsing paths. Current state: multiple services import different JWT parsers and SAML XML libs leading to inconsistent validation, duplicated signature verification code, and fragile error handling that has allowed parsing edge cases in token processing. Goals: 1) provide a single internal crypto-abstraction layer with a clear public API for token validation, signing, and certificate management; 2) upgrade OpenSSL to 3.0.8+ (security backports) with FIPS-compatible build as an opt-in flag for Private deployments; 3) replace ad-hoc SAML consumers with a hardened parser wrapper that centralizes XML signature verification and entity validation; 4) run extended fuzzing and CVE regression tests in CI to catch token parsing regressions before rollout.
acceptance_criteria: All services in services/auth/* use the new crypto-abstraction API and no longer import internal-legacy-jwt or ad-hoc saml-xml-utils
OpenSSL upgraded to 3.0.8+ in standard images and a FIPS-enabled build published to the image registry for Private customers
SAML assertion parsing has canonicalization + strict namespace checks and passes the new saml-fuzz CI job with zero regressions
Automated end-to-end tests validate JWT edge cases (leading/trailing whitespace, unusual unicode, nested claims) and are green in canary cluster
Security sign-off completed (security_review_required = true) with documented remediation of all CVEs addressed by the upgrade
implementation_notes: Introduce packages/crypto-abstraction with minimal surface: verify_jwt(token, opts), sign_jwt(payload, key_id), verify_saml(assertion, idp_metadata)
Add a buildmatrix job that builds two runtime images: runtime:openssl-3.0 and runtime:openssl-3.0-fips; publish both to container registry with tags
Migrate services incrementally: auth-service -> session-service -> gateway-proxy. Each migration includes feature flag to switch verification path for 2 weeks of traffic monitoring
Where possible reuse existing public key caches (KMS-backed JWKS caching) and add circuit breaker to avoid accidental DoS during key rotation
Maintain a compatibility shim for legacy tokens during transition period (30 days) that logs occurrences to a dedicated telemetry stream for manual review
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): deploy new runtime:openssl-3.0 image to canary cluster for auth-service only; enable feature flag for 5% traffic; monitor latency and error rate for 72h
Phase 1 (service migrations): sequentially switch session-service and gateway-proxy behind feature flags; each service observed for 48h before continuing
Phase 2 (FIPS images): publish FIPS image and coordinate with two Private customers to validate in their staging environments; address platform packaging and KMS policies
Phase 3 (global): remove compatibility shim after 30-day overlap and cut a platform-2026.04 release for all infra images
risks: Token parsing changes could cause drop-in incompatibilities with older clients that send non-standard JWTs; mitigated by compatibility shim and telemetry
OpenSSL FIPS build changes ABI which might break some native extensions; mitigation: build and smoke test all native modules against FIPS image in CI
SAML parser hardening could reject IdPs with malformed metadata; mitigation: provide an opt-out temporary relax mode and run a discovery scan of configured enterprise IdPs before enforcement
Dependency upgrade may surface transitive license flags; coordinate legal/OSS review early
